paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
paper.source_locator: Section 5 'A simulation study', arXiv:2304.10025v4 PDF page 23: the displayed data-generating process for (X, Z, D, M, Y). ITT-NIE and ITT-NDE are defined on PDF page 23 just above that display (ratio scale shown there; the paper states it primarily works on the mean-difference scale).

mechanism.name: Intention-to-treat natural direct effect with a post-treatment event in a Kang-Schafer style design

generation_equations.label: Post-treatment event
generation_equations.expression: D | Z, X ~ Bernoulli(expit(-1 + 2 Z + [1, -0.8, 0.6, -1]^T X))

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; X, then Z, then D, then M, then Y are generated in temporal order within an individual

assumptions: Consistency and well-defined interventions on Z and M
Randomized Z given X, as encoded by the printed propensity model
Mediator-outcome exchangeability given (Z, D, X); the post-treatment event D must be adjusted for
The cross-world condition required for the natural effect contrast

Positivity: the source deliberately builds a Kang-Schafer style design in which positivity is PRACTICALLY violated under model misspecification, so finite-sample overlap is poor by design even though every probability is strictly inside (0,1) for finite X
The registered target depends only on the marginal laws of D(1), D(0), M(1) and M(0); it does not require the joint counterfactual law of (D(1), D(0)), which this mechanism does not specify

properties.notes: Four baseline covariates X1..X4 ~ N(0, I4); all four enter the Z, D, M and Y equations with nonzero coefficients, so dimension = effective_dimension = 4. The post-treatment event D is not counted as a baseline covariate. Not high dimensional: p = 4 against the source sample size n = 1000. No product term appears in any structural equation, so interactions = false. nonlinear = true for the three logistic links only; the outcome mean is linear in (Z, D, M, X). The source's transformed covariates, which are strongly nonlinear, belong to its misspecified working models and not to this mechanism.

estimand.name: ITT-NDE = E[Y_{1 M_0}] - E[Y_{0 M_0}]
estimand.definition: Intention-to-treat natural direct effect of the randomized treatment Z with mediator M, in a design that also contains a post-treatment event D (for example noncompliance). Setting Z = z lets the post-treatment event take D(z), while the mediator is held at M(0). This is NOT the principal-stratum quantity theta^(10)_10 that the source plots, NOT an indirect effect, and NOT a complier average causal effect.

truth.expression: Intention-to-treat natural direct effect of the randomized treatment Z with mediator M, in a design that also contains a post-treatment event D (for example noncompliance). Setting Z = z lets the post-treatment event take D(z), while the mediator is held at M(0). This is NOT the principal-stratum quantity theta^(10)_10 that the source plots, NOT an indirect effect, and NOT a complier average causal effect.
truth.derivation: Two-dimensional Gauss-Hermite quadrature. The two linear predictors a_D^T X and a_M^T X are jointly normal with variances 3.00 and 3.06 and covariance 2.94, so E[D(z)] and E[M(z)] reduce to bivariate integrals; the outcome is linear in Z, D, M and X, hence ITT-NDE = 1.5 - (E[D(1)] - E[D(0)]). Orders 80 and 160 are compared to bound the quadrature error.

adaptations: Version used: arXiv:2304.10025v4 (2024-09-13) preprint; the published journal version was not accessible to the collector, so section and page locators refer to the preprint PDF and journal pages 1-22 were not cross-checked.

REGISTERED TARGET IS NOT THE SOURCE'S FIGURE 2 TARGET. The source's Figure 2 reports the principal-stratum quantity theta^(10)_10 = E[Y_{1 M_0} | U = 10], which conditions on the principal stratum U = (D(1), D(0)) = (1, 0). The printed equations give only the conditional law of D given (Z, X); they do NOT specify the joint counterfactual law of (D(1), D(0)), so theta^(10)_10 is not determined by the display alone and is deliberately not registered. The registered target is instead the source's own population-level ITT natural direct effect on the mean-difference scale, which depends only on marginal counterfactual means and is therefore fully determined by the display.

The source states the generating process is 'modified from that in Kang and Schafer (2007)'. The transformed covariates Xtilde1 = exp(0.5 X1), Xtilde2 = X2/(1 + X1), Xtilde3 = (X2 X3/25 + 0.6)^3, Xtilde4 = (X2 + X4 + 20)^2 are an estimation device fed to misspecified working models; they are NOT part of the data-generating mechanism and are not generated or exported here.

The source generates 1000 Monte Carlo samples of size 1000 and compares four moment-type estimators, a multiply robust estimator and a cross-fitted nonparametric estimator under six misspecification scenarios; none of that estimation work is reproduced.

Truth method: the source does not print a numerical truth. The registered value is derived by the collector with two-dimensional Gauss-Hermite quadrature over the bivariate normal law of the two linear predictors, and must be checked by a reviewer.
Sampling is re-implemented with NumPy Generator(PCG64); no attempt is made to match the source software draw-for-draw.
